import pandas as pd

# List of source file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/training_8.csv"
]

# Columns of the target schema
target_columns = ['created_at', 'text', 'coordinates', 'hashtags']

# Read all source CSVs into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in the same order
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# UNION operation: concatenate all DataFrames vertically
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure data types match target examples:
# - created_at: string (keep as is, pandas reads as object/string)
# - text: string
# - coordinates: string (some are dict-like or NaN, convert all to string)
# - hashtags: string (some are lists or dict-lists, convert all to string)

# Convert 'coordinates' column to string, replacing NaN with 'NaN' string for consistency
target_df['coordinates'] = target_df['coordinates'].apply(lambda x: str(x) if pd.notna(x) else 'NaN')

# Convert 'hashtags' column to string, replacing NaN with '[]' string if any
def hashtags_to_str(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return '[]'
    # If already a string, keep as is
    if isinstance(x, str):
        return x
    # If list or dict, convert to string
    return str(x)

target_df['hashtags'] = target_df['hashtags'].apply(hashtags_to_str)

# Convert 'created_at' and 'text' to string explicitly (in case of any anomalies)
target_df['created_at'] = target_df['created_at'].astype(str)
target_df['text'] = target_df['text'].astype(str)

# Write the resulting DataFrame to the target CSV path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_16/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
